_note: Rendered by the site's institution map. Edit text freely. pos = map coordinates. variants = only shown when the reader's Q1/Q4 setting matches. Edge kinds feed the overlays: accountability (elects, delegates, appoints, removes, vetoes, checks, barred), money (funds), information (informs, audits, oversees, refers). directs and negotiates show in the structure view.

nodes.summary: Every resident voter. All powers derive from the people and are exercised only through the bodies below.
powers: Vote in every election and referendum
Stand for any office as an individual
Recall any elected or delegated office-holder (20% petition)
Initiate laws and amendments (100,000 signatures)
Take part in their local assembly and workplace council
Direct their media voucher to news organisations of their choice
nodes.composition: Citizens aged 16+ and residents of five years or more

nodes.summary: Elected each year by the workers of every social enterprise, public body and larger private firm. They appoint management and organise the work.
powers: Appoint and dismiss the management of socially owned enterprises
Approve the enterprise plan and budget
Decide work organisation, safety and job rotation
Handle peer accountability with fair procedures
Federate by sector and county
nodes.composition: All workers of the enterprise; council elected by secret ballot
nodes.selection: Annual election of individuals (no party lists)
nodes.recall: At any time by the workforce

safeguards.mechanism: Self-management has a constitutional floor (Art. 34) and its own federation, independent of the State and of any party.

precedent.text: Russian factory committees, 1917, subordinated and replaced by one-man management in 1918

safeguards.residual_risk: Councils can become rubber stamps for management or for the most organised faction. Turnout in workplace elections may fall over time (FM-08).

strongest_critique.liberal: Workers are not the only stakeholders. Giving them control over firms that serve the public can sacrifice users' interests to insiders'.
strongest_critique.market: Firms run by their workers under-invest and under-hire: the Yugoslav evidence on income-per-member maximisation.
strongest_critique.left: Council communists would say a council that sits inside a state-planned economy with a leading party is self-management in name only.

safeguards.mechanism: Rotation of unpleasant tasks and peer handling of shirking (Arts. 73, 75) replace both Stakhanovite norm-raising and indifference.
safeguards.residual_risk: Peer pressure can become bullying. Rotation costs skill and efficiency.

strongest_critique.liberal: Peer discipline without outside appeal is a recipe for petty tyranny.
strongest_critique.market: Rotation destroys returns to specialisation.
strongest_critique.left: 'Accountability to peers' still means workers policing each other on capital's old productivity terms.

nodes.summary: Independent of the State and of every party, with the right to strike, including against the State.
powers: Organise workers
Bargain collectively, including with public and socially owned enterprises
Strike, including against the State itself

safeguards.mechanism: Constitutional independence and the right to strike against the State (Art. 11.2). A workers' state that forbids independent workers' organisation has stopped being one.
safeguards.residual_risk: Unions can become sectional, defending insiders against outsiders and users. A general strike against an elected government poses a real legitimacy conflict (see the stress test).

strongest_critique.liberal: Unions with a constitutional right to strike against the State can hold the public hostage.
strongest_critique.market: Union power in socially owned firms reproduces the soft budget constraint: strikes win rescues.
strongest_critique.left: In a 'workers' state' the bureaucracy will treat strikes as sabotage regardless of the text. Only independent organisation, not a clause, protects them.

nodes.summary: A new parish or ward tier (2,000–10,000 residents) open to every resident. It allocates at least a third of the county's capital budget.
powers: Allocate their share of at least a third of the county capital budget
Elect delegates to the county council
Summon any local official to answer questions
nodes.composition: All residents aged 16+; standing committee chosen by lot each year

safeguards.mechanism: A constitutionally fixed share of the capital budget (Art. 57), so the assembly cannot be kept as a shell while its money is quietly removed.

precedent.text: Kerala People's Plan Campaign: 35–40% of the plan budget devolved
Porto Alegre after 2004: kept in name, starved of money

safeguards.residual_risk: Attendance skews toward the retired, the confident and the organised. Meeting fatigue sets in.

strongest_critique.liberal: Open assemblies are dominated by whoever turns up; they have no clear accountability and no protection for absent minorities.
strongest_critique.market: Fragmenting capital budgets across hundreds of wards destroys economies of scale and coherent infrastructure planning.
strongest_critique.left: Participatory budgeting can become a way to make communities manage scarcity themselves, as in Porto Alegre's later years.

safeguards.mechanism: A standing committee chosen by lot each year prepares business, so the same activists do not control the agenda year after year.
safeguards.residual_risk: Committee members chosen by lot depend on council staff for information.

strongest_critique.liberal: Lot gives power to people who did not seek it and answer to no one.

nodes.summary: The people decide every constitutional amendment and can initiate laws with 100,000 signatures. The Citizens' Chamber can force a referendum on any Act.
powers: Approve every constitutional amendment
Decide citizen-initiated laws not enacted by the Assembly
Decide Acts referred by the Citizens' Chamber
Decide the party's status every ten years (Q1 default)

safeguards.mechanism: The people keep the final word on the constitution. Social ownership can be changed only by two Assemblies with an election between and then a referendum.
safeguards.residual_risk: Referendums reward simple messages and well-funded campaigns. Equal public funding (Art. 41.2) helps but does not remove this.

strongest_critique.liberal: Direct democracy can override minority rights; the eternity clause covers only the democratic core.
strongest_critique.market: Voters cannot weigh complex economic trade-offs in a yes/no vote.
strongest_critique.left: Plebiscites have often legitimised strong executives rather than restraining them.

nodes.summary: Runs every election and referendum, regulates campaign finance, draws boundaries, and registers parties as Q1 requires.
powers: Conduct elections and referendums
Maintain the register
Regulate campaign finance
Draw constituency boundaries
Register parties (and apply to the Constitutional Court to refuse registration, under Q1-B)
nodes.recall: Removal only for misbehaviour by 2/3 of the Assembly after a court finding

safeguards.mechanism: Independence, a budget fixed by formula for five years, and protection against removal (Art. 98).
safeguards.residual_risk: Whoever draws boundaries and registers parties can tilt the field, especially under Q1-B.

strongest_critique.liberal: A single commission policing political speech in campaigns is a dangerous concentration of power.
strongest_critique.left: Electoral bodies inherit the assumptions of whoever designed them.

nodes.summary: 120 residents chosen by lot, half renewed each year. It has binding power exactly where elected politicians have a conflict of interest.
powers: Set officials' pay and permitted benefits (via the Pay and Privileges Panel)
Approve or refuse any extension of an emergency
Oversee the security services (via the Security Oversight Committee)
Force a referendum on any Act (2/3 vote within 60 days)
Audit the party's internal elections and finances (Q1)
Set the topics of citizens' assemblies
Hire and rotate its own secretariat
nodes.composition: 120 residents chosen by lot, stratified by county, sex, age and class
nodes.recall: Removal only by the Chamber itself, 2/3, for misconduct

safeguards.mechanism: Nobody sets their own pay. Pay and privileges are fixed and audited by people chosen by lot, who cannot build a career on it.

precedent.text: Athens: the Council of 500 by lot

safeguards.residual_risk: Members may be overawed by officials and defer to them.

strongest_critique.liberal: People chosen by lot answer to no electorate. Binding power without accountability is power without legitimacy.
strongest_critique.market: Amateurs setting public-sector pay will cause shortages of skilled staff.
strongest_critique.left: A randomly chosen body can be steered by whoever briefs it, and lot can become a depoliticising substitute for organised class power.

safeguards.mechanism: A binding veto on extending emergencies, and full-access security oversight by a body that no one can capture by winning an election.

precedent.text: Weimar Article 48: emergency rule without effective check

safeguards.residual_risk: In a real crisis a body chosen by lot may defer to the executive's account of the threat.

strongest_critique.liberal: Security decisions need expertise and secrecy, and lot provides neither.

safeguards.mechanism: Binding powers in bounded areas: advisory assemblies fade, as Ireland's own experience shows.
safeguards.residual_risk: Secretariat capture. Clause 39.3 (the Chamber hires and rotates its own staff) is the counter, and it is not proven.

strongest_critique.market: Bounded binding powers may still produce gridlock when the Chamber forces referendums on contested economic Acts.

nodes.summary: Ad hoc assemblies of 99–150 people chosen by lot, on topics set by the Chamber, the Assembly or 50,000 citizens. The Assembly must answer within six months.
powers: Deliberate and recommend
Recommendations not adopted within two years can be sent to referendum by the Citizens' Chamber

safeguards.mechanism: A duty to respond with reasons, and an escalation route to referendum, so recommendations cannot simply lapse.

precedent.text: Convention on the Constitution, 2012–14; Citizens' Assembly 2016–18

safeguards.residual_risk: Agenda-setting and expert selection still shape outcomes.

strongest_critique.left: Assemblies can launder decisions already taken elsewhere.

nodes.summary: 21 members of the Citizens' Chamber chosen by lot each year. They fix the skilled worker's wage for all office-holders and audit asset declarations.
powers: Fix the office-holders' wage and permitted benefits (binding)
Audit annual declarations of assets and interests
Refer breaches to the courts

safeguards.mechanism: Officials are paid a skilled worker's wage, in money only, with no benefit in kind unavailable to every resident. They use the same public services. Declarations are public.

precedent.text: Paris Commune: 'public service … at workman's wage'
Voslensky on nomenklatura privileges in kind

safeguards.residual_risk: Privilege moves into informal networks: access, favours, family connections. The Standards Commission has to follow it there.

strongest_critique.liberal: Capping pay for judges, doctors-in-office and top managers will drive talent abroad in an open EU labour market.
strongest_critique.market: Pay caps will produce under-the-table compensation, as Soviet experience shows.
strongest_critique.left: Equalising officials' pay doesn't touch the deeper source of bureaucratic power: control of information and appointments.

nodes.summary: The workplace councils federated by sector and county, independent of the State and of any party. It sends delegates to the Congress of Councils and the National Investment Council.
powers: Coordinate workplace councils
Send mandated delegates to the Congress of Councils and the National Investment Council

safeguards.mechanism: Self-management federated through its own structures, not through the State or a party.

precedent.text: All-Russian Congress of Factory Committees, never held (anarchist-leaning account)

safeguards.residual_risk: Federations develop their own full-time apparatus (Michels).

strongest_critique.liberal: A producers' federation with a role in national planning entrenches producer interests over consumers.
strongest_critique.market: Sectoral federations bargain for their sector, reproducing soft budget pressures.

nodes.summary: Two thirds elected by STV, one third delegated by local assemblies. They run local services, planning, housing allocation and policing priorities, and hire their own chief executive.
powers: Govern local services, planning and housing allocation
Set local policing priorities
Appoint and dismiss the chief executive
Send delegates to the Congress of Councils and regional planning boards
nodes.recall: Yes, by electors or delegating assemblies

safeguards.mechanism: This reverses the 2014 split that left real power with appointed chief executives. Recall and delegation tie the council to its localities.
safeguards.residual_risk: County politics can become clientelist, which is a long Irish tradition.

strongest_critique.market: Local control of planning invites NIMBY blockage of housing and renewables.

nodes.summary: The only organisation that may run candidates under a party label. It has no reserved seats, no veto and no command over any state body, and must win against independents at every election.
powers: Nominate candidates under a party label
Receive public funding as an electoral organisation
Organise, publish and campaign
nodes.composition: Voluntary membership; protected internal platforms and factions
nodes.selection: Internal secret ballots; internal bodies by proportional representation
nodes.recall: Internal; renewal referendum every 10 years on its status

safeguards.mechanism: Factions and platforms legally protected inside the party (Art. 31), the direct reversal of the 1921 ban, so disagreement stays visible and organised.
safeguards.residual_risk: Factions protected on paper are not safe in practice when careers depend on the leadership's favour.

strongest_critique.liberal: One party, however internally plural, denies citizens the right to organise an electoral alternative. Internal pluralism is no substitute for external competition.
strongest_critique.left: Every ruling party began with internal democracy. The Bolsheviks had factions until 1921. Rules do not survive a crisis; only the balance of forces does.

safeguards.mechanism: Party–state separation: no one holds senior party and state office at once, and the party is barred from commanding police, intelligence, defence, courts or audit (Art. 32).

precedent.text: Cheka as 'direct agencies of the Party'
Voslensky: nomenklatura and security under the Central Committee

safeguards.residual_risk: Loyal non-office-holders can be placed in state posts. The audit by lot must look at networks.

strongest_critique.liberal: Separation on paper is easily evaded by informal channels.

safeguards.mechanism: Its role is never guaranteed by law: independents can win every seat. *Drafter's addition:* a referendum every ten years on its status (Art. 33).

precedent.text: Uganda's 'no-party' Movement system (shows how organised incumbents win)

safeguards.residual_risk: **Thinnest safeguard in the design.** An organised party competing against unorganised individuals wins most contests. A pro-market minority has speech but no electoral vehicle and may lose faith in the system or go underground (FM-10).

strongest_critique.liberal: This is a one-party state with good manners.
strongest_critique.market: Without competition between parties, policy errors go uncorrected for longer.
strongest_critique.left: A leading role must be earned in struggle. Constitutionalising even a party's *ballot label* monopoly invites careerists.

nodes.summary: Any party that accepts the democratic core and core social ownership may register and stand. Only the Constitutional Court may refuse registration, and only on narrow grounds.
powers: Nominate candidates
Receive public funding (weighted toward small and new parties)

safeguards.mechanism: A split becomes a new party, not a crisis. The line is drawn by a court on narrow, published grounds, never by the governing party.
safeguards.residual_risk: The June 1918 expulsions were justified as defence against counter-revolution. Whoever controls the court defines 'socialist'.

strongest_critique.liberal: Banning parties by programme is incompatible with liberal democracy.
strongest_critique.left: Pro-capitalist politics will return under socialist labels.

nodes.summary: Associations campaign freely but cannot nominate candidates or run slates. Candidates stand as individuals, and the Citizens' Chamber may initiate legislation.
powers: Publish, campaign and endorse ideas

safeguards.mechanism: No party machine controls nominations.
safeguards.residual_risk: 'No parties' tends to mean one hidden party. Informal slates form with less transparency.

strongest_critique.market: Voters lose the information shortcut that party programmes provide.
strongest_critique.left: The best-organised existing network wins by default.

nodes.summary: 160 members elected by STV for four years, individually recallable. It makes laws, elects and can recall the Executive Council at any time, and approves the plan and budget.
powers: Make laws
Elect and recall the Executive Council at any time
Approve the national plan (with the Congress of Councils) and the budget
Approve or annul emergency declarations
Set the physical ecological budgets by law

safeguards.mechanism: It can recall the executive at any time without dissolving itself (Art. 44), so recall is cheap and carries no penalty.
safeguards.residual_risk: Easy recall can mean unstable government and short-termism.

strongest_critique.liberal: An executive that can be recalled at any time has no independent mandate to resist a passing majority.
strongest_critique.market: Unstable executives cannot make credible long-term commitments to investors or planners.

safeguards.mechanism: Term limits (two consecutive terms, ten years in any office), a skilled worker's wage, and asset declarations.
safeguards.residual_risk: Term limits drain expertise and empower permanent staff.

strongest_critique.liberal: Term limits disempower voters who want to re-elect a good representative.

nodes.summary: Directly elected for a single seven-year term. Ceremonial guardian with the power to refer Bills to the Constitutional Court.
powers: Refer Bills to the Constitutional Court
Convene the Assembly if the Executive fails to
Appoint judges on the Judicial Appointments Commission's nomination

safeguards.mechanism: One non-renewable term and no executive power: continuity without a seat of power.
safeguards.residual_risk: A popular president can use moral authority to campaign against the government.

strongest_critique.left: A head of state is a monarchical relic.

nodes.summary: Nine judges on single, staggered 12-year terms. It reviews laws on referral or individual complaint, enforces social rights, and reviews the Ecological Authority's vetoes.
powers: Strike down unconstitutional laws and acts
Enforce social rights with structural orders and timetables
Rule on party registration (Q1-B)
Review Ecological Authority vetoes on points of law
Rule on whether an emergency has a factual basis

safeguards.mechanism: Independent courts are part of the eternal democratic core. Fusing the judiciary into the governing body is how emergency powers became permanent.
safeguards.residual_risk: Courts can be packed slowly through appointments. Staggered single terms and the mixed appointments commission are the counter.

strongest_critique.market: Justiciable social rights let judges make budget decisions they are not equipped for.
strongest_critique.left: Unelected judges recruited from the legal profession will strike down socialist legislation, as US courts did in the Lochner era.

nodes.summary: Judges, practising lawyers and members of the public chosen by lot, in equal thirds. It nominates every judge. No politician sits on it.
powers: Nominate all judges
nodes.composition: Judges, lawyers and lay members chosen by lot, in equal numbers

safeguards.mechanism: Appointment is taken out of executive hands, with lay members chosen by lot against a closed professional caste.

precedent.text: Ireland's Judicial Appointments Commission reforms (to be sourced)

safeguards.residual_risk: The profession's members may dominate the lay third.

strongest_critique.left: Self-selecting judiciaries reproduce their own class background.

nodes.summary: Equal numbers of delegates from county councils and the Federation of Workplace Councils. It co-approves the investment plan and can propose laws that the Assembly must vote on.
powers: Co-approve the national investment plan
Propose laws (the Assembly must vote within 90 days)
nodes.composition: County and workplace delegates in equal numbers

safeguards.mechanism: A second, council-based channel alongside direct election, never the only channel, unlike Soviet multi-tier indirect elections.
safeguards.residual_risk: Delegation through tiers distances the base from decisions.

strongest_critique.liberal: Two chambers with different bases invites deadlock on the plan.
strongest_critique.market: Producer-weighted representation biases investment toward existing industries.

nodes.summary: Negotiates the five-year investment plan among workers, users, counties and the executive. The Ecological Authority sits without a vote but holds a veto.
powers: Prepare the five-year investment plan by negotiation
Coordinate the regional planning boards
nodes.composition: Delegates of the Federation, users' councils, county councils and the Executive; Ecological Authority (no vote)

safeguards.mechanism: Negotiated coordination (Devine): market exchange for current output, negotiation for capacity. No single planning centre.

precedent.text: Hayek, 'The Use of Knowledge in Society'

safeguards.residual_risk: Negotiation bodies can become a coordinator class (FM-01). Devine's model is thin on operational detail.

strongest_critique.liberal: Committees negotiating investment will allocate by political weight, not returns.
strongest_critique.market: Hayek: the knowledge needed is local and tacit, and no negotiating council can gather it. Without capital markets there is no price for capital.
strongest_critique.left: Negotiated coordination is corporatism with a socialist vocabulary.

safeguards.mechanism: Open books (Art. 59): the plan's data and every enterprise's accounts are public.
safeguards.residual_risk: Data can be published but not understood. Open data favours those with analysts.

nodes.summary: Seven members elected by the Assembly by proportional representation, recallable at any time. It decides collectively, and the chair rotates yearly.
powers: Direct the public service and departments
Lawfully direct police and Defence Forces (as a body only)
Declare an emergency (72 hours unless the Assembly approves)
Negotiate foreign charters and EU exemptions
nodes.selection: Elected by the Assembly by PR
nodes.term: Recallable at any time; Art. 28 limits
nodes.recall: Assembly majority, any time, no dissolution

safeguards.mechanism: A collective executive with a rotating chair (first among equals): no single office for a cult to grow around.
safeguards.residual_risk: Collective leadership can be slow and indecisive in a crisis. Charisma can still dominate from inside a collective.

strongest_critique.liberal: Diffuse responsibility means nobody is accountable for failures.
strongest_critique.left: The Politburo was also formally collective.

safeguards.mechanism: A skilled worker's wage, the same public services as everyone, and published declarations (Art. 28).
safeguards.residual_risk: Informal privilege (access, networks).

strongest_critique.market: Underpaying ministers lowers the quality of government.

nodes.summary: Independent courts with jury trial. They alone may impose penalties or deprive liberty. Judges issue every surveillance warrant.
powers: Try every offence
Issue intercept and surveillance warrants
Annul emergency orders
Hear whistle-blower and dissent cases

safeguards.mechanism: No tribunal outside the courts may punish, and no offence may be defined by opinion or allegiance: no 'counter-revolution' charge.
safeguards.residual_risk: Courts can be overwhelmed or intimidated in a real crisis.

strongest_critique.left: Bourgeois legality protects saboteurs as well as dissidents. That is the point, and it is also the risk.

nodes.summary: Investigates conflicts of interest, cooling-off breaches and networks of influence that do not appear in formal posts.
powers: Investigate conflicts of interest and networks of influence
Refer breaches to the courts

safeguards.mechanism: It follows privilege into informal networks once formal privilege is abolished.

precedent.text: Voslensky; Kotz & Weir on elite conversion of control into ownership

safeguards.residual_risk: Investigating 'networks' can become a political weapon.

strongest_critique.liberal: Investigating informal relationships is intrusive and open to abuse.

nodes.summary: Default (Q4-B): Ireland stays a member and negotiates exemptions, with a published Fallback Schedule. Switch Q4 to see the 'leave' and 'defy' paths.

summary_variants.Q4=C: Under Q4-C Ireland leaves the Union under Article 50. The EU becomes a trading partner, and Northern Ireland stays inside its goods market.
summary_variants.Q4=D: Under Q4-D Ireland stays a member but openly declines to comply with specific rules, accepting infringement proceedings.

powers: Single market, competition and state-aid law
Euro and ECB monetary policy
Rule-of-law oversight (Art. 7 TEU)

safeguards.mechanism: Membership keeps market access (82% public support), an outside rule-of-law check, and state-aid rules that harden budget constraints. Exemptions are sought openly. Any refusal to comply follows a Fallback Schedule published and approved in advance.
safeguards.residual_risk: Treaty change needs unanimity, so exemptions may never come. A published fallback can be priced in by markets. The Q1 default (one party label) may be challenged under Art. 2 TEU.

strongest_critique.liberal: A state that pre-announces where it would break the law has already undermined legal certainty.
strongest_critique.market: Staying in the single market leaves most planning tools out of reach.
strongest_critique.left: The EU's economic constitution is neoliberal by design. Negotiating exemptions from it is reformism.

nodes.summary: Constituted like the National Investment Council, they plan investment within each region and weight it toward regional need.
powers: Plan regional investment within the national plan
Weight investment by regional need
nodes.composition: Workplace, user, county and executive delegates

safeguards.mechanism: Investment is steered by regional need, not only by enterprise surplus, against Yugoslavia's widening gap (Slovenia 2.5% unemployment, Kosovo 21% in 1965).
safeguards.residual_risk: Regional boards bargain against each other for national money.

strongest_critique.market: Spreading investment by region rather than return wastes capital.
strongest_critique.left: Regional planning bodies became vehicles for republic-level elites in Yugoslavia.

nodes.summary: At least half its members are elected by farmers. It negotiates the land-use plan and the herd transition, with income guarantees.
powers: Negotiate the national land-use plan
Administer income guarantees and stewardship payments
Return processing to co-operative ownership
nodes.composition: At least half elected by farmers; also processing workers, the Ecological Authority and the Executive

safeguards.mechanism: The herd transition is negotiated with farmers rather than imposed, with income guaranteed at the household's five-year average, and family farms protected from collectivisation without consent.

precedent.text: CSO herd 6.9m; agriculture 38% of emissions; €10.7bn beef and dairy exports

safeguards.residual_risk: Farmers' delegates may block reduction indefinitely. The board then faces the Ecological Authority's veto, which is a real conflict without an easy resolution.

strongest_critique.liberal: Guaranteeing income pegged to boom-year cattle prices is very expensive.
strongest_critique.market: Paying farmers to stop farming creates dependency and leaves land idle.
strongest_critique.left: Protecting family farms entrenches a conservative petty-proprietor class (the Land Acts' own legacy).

nodes.summary: Recruited on merit by an independent Public Appointments Commission. There is no list of posts needing party or political approval.
powers: Administer departments under the Executive Council
Refuse unlawful instructions

safeguards.mechanism: There is no nomenklatura list: appointments below the Executive are on merit, with a duty to refuse unlawful instructions.
safeguards.residual_risk: A merit-based permanent service becomes its own caste (Michels; Trotsky's 'policeman').

strongest_critique.market: Without market discipline, public administration expands (Parkinson; Kornai).
strongest_critique.left: A permanent civil service is exactly the bureaucracy Marx wanted the Commune to dissolve.

nodes.summary: 12 members of the Citizens' Chamber chosen by lot, 4 Assembly members chosen by lot from outside the Executive and the largest grouping, and a judge-Inspector. It has full access and can suspend operations.
powers: Full access to the records, premises and staff of the police, intelligence and Defence Forces
Publish findings
Suspend unlawful operations pending the High Court
Review all surveillance warrants
nodes.composition: 12 by lot from the Citizens' Chamber + 4 Assembly members (not Executive or largest grouping) + Inspector

safeguards.mechanism: Oversight by a body that cannot be captured by winning an election, with full access and the power to suspend operations.

precedent.text: Cheka answerable only to the party

safeguards.residual_risk: Members chosen by lot may defer to security professionals. The Inspector and full access are the counterweight, and they are not proven.

strongest_critique.liberal: Leaks from lay overseers endanger operations and sources.
strongest_critique.left: Oversight legitimises the existence of a secret service that a workers' democracy should not have at all.

nodes.summary: Investigates complaints against any public body or socially owned enterprise, including complaints from users' councils.
powers: Investigate complaints
Enter premises and see records
Publish reports

safeguards.mechanism: Gives every resident a free route to challenge the administration, so grievances do not simply accumulate.
safeguards.residual_risk: Reports are ignored if they have no binding force.

nodes.summary: Audits every public body, socially owned enterprise, charter enterprise and funded party, and reports publicly to the Assembly and the Citizens' Chamber.
powers: Audit all public money
Report publicly
Support the Pay and Privileges Panel
nodes.composition: Comptroller and Auditor General and staff

safeguards.mechanism: Independent audit with a budget fixed by formula. The party is barred from instructing it (Art. 32).

precedent.text: Kornai: soft budgets need visibility to harden

safeguards.residual_risk: Audit sees accounts, not informal power.

nodes.summary: The grid, water, rail, housing construction, energy generation and other strategic sectors. Boards are one third workers, one third users and communities, and one third appointed. Budgets are hard.
powers: Run strategic sectors
Appoint management through workplace councils

safeguards.mechanism: The housing stock, grid, water, health and rail can be privatised only by two Assemblies with an election between, then a referendum (Art. 109).

precedent.text: Kotz & Weir: privatisation by the elite

safeguards.residual_risk: Entrenchment is a secondary defence: Weimar shows gains hold only while the balance of forces does.

strongest_critique.liberal: Locking sectors into public ownership freezes economic structure against future needs.

safeguards.mechanism: Hard budgets: a rescue is a public, costed vote, never automatic. Users sit on the board.
safeguards.residual_risk: Political pressure to rescue large local employers.

strongest_critique.market: Public enterprises always face softer budgets than private ones, whatever the rules say.
strongest_critique.left: Tripartite boards reproduce management-labour bargaining under a new name.

nodes.summary: Worker, consumer and producer co-ops. Membership opens after at most a year's probation, non-member staff are capped at 10%, reserves are indivisible, and there is no demutualisation.
powers: Produce and trade in markets
Govern themselves by one member, one vote

safeguards.mechanism: Rules against insider capture: compulsory admission after probation, a 10% cap on non-member staff, indivisible reserves, and no conversion to shareholder companies.
safeguards.residual_risk: Compulsory membership dilutes commitment. Indivisible reserves weaken members' willingness to invest.

strongest_critique.liberal: Forcing co-ops to admit members limits their freedom of association.
strongest_critique.market: Co-ops under hard budgets in competitive markets drift toward capitalist behaviour.
strongest_critique.left: Co-ops in markets self-exploit; market socialism is still market discipline.

nodes.summary: Family firms, shops, cafés, trades and family farms with up to 50 employees. Workers have the right of first offer when a business is sold or its owner retires.
powers: Trade freely in markets

safeguards.mechanism: Variety and responsiveness where planning is weakest: no Trabant queues, no Intershop.
safeguards.residual_risk: Private enterprise creates a constituency for restoration (FM-12) and market inequality.

strongest_critique.liberal: A 50-employee cap stunts successful firms and drives them abroad.
strongest_critique.left: Petty capitalism is the seedbed of capitalist restoration.

nodes.summary: Builds, owns and maintains public housing at cost rent for all, not only the poor, to high design standards, allocated by published rules.
powers: Build and maintain public housing
Allocate by published rules
Share management with tenants' councils
nodes.composition: Board under Art. 48 model; tenants' councils

safeguards.mechanism: Universal cost-rent housing and published allocation rules: no queue for a 'policeman' to control, and no priority for office-holders.
safeguards.residual_risk: Build-out takes a decade, and allocation queues will exist meanwhile.

strongest_critique.market: Cost rent with no market signal under-prices good locations and misallocates housing.

nodes.summary: A single-tier public service, free at the point of use. Nobody can buy faster access to public facilities.
powers: Provide health care free at the point of use

safeguards.mechanism: Single tier: no paid queue-jumping in public facilities, and no special clinics for officials.
safeguards.residual_risk: Private practice outside public facilities remains, which keeps an informal second tier.

strongest_critique.market: Free at the point of use with no price signal means rationing by waiting.
strongest_critique.left: Allowing private practice at all preserves two-tier care.

nodes.summary: A civilian police service with no political function. Counties set local priorities, and officers have a duty to refuse unlawful orders, including against peaceful protest or strikes.
powers: Policing under law

safeguards.mechanism: No political policing; a duty to refuse unlawful orders; independent complaints; oversight by lot.

precedent.text: Commune police as 'responsible and revocable agent'

safeguards.residual_risk: Police culture is resistant to change. Riot policing in a general strike is the real test.

strongest_critique.left: The police remain a special body of armed men separate from the people.

nodes.name_ga: An tÚdarás Póilíneachta agus Ombudsman na bPóilíní
nodes.summary: Independent oversight of national policing policy, and independent investigation of every complaint and every death or serious injury involving the police.
powers: Oversee policing policy
Investigate complaints independently

safeguards.mechanism: Police are never investigated by police.
safeguards.residual_risk: Under-resourced investigators defer to the force.

nodes.summary: Ensures that the accounts, plans, contracts and input–output data of every public body and socially owned enterprise are public and usable.
powers: Enforce publication
Publish the State's data

safeguards.mechanism: Open books against both Djilas (control hidden behind ownership) and Hayek (planners monopolising knowledge).
safeguards.residual_risk: Data is published but not used; or it is used mostly by those with analysts.

strongest_critique.liberal: Full transparency of enterprise data destroys commercial confidentiality.

nodes.summary: Multinationals operating under charters approved by the Assembly that fix tax, workplace-council rights, ecological budgets and training. No expropriation without compensation.
powers: Operate under charter

safeguards.mechanism: The FDI model is changed openly and by stages, not ended overnight. Windfall tax is ring-fenced first.

precedent.text: Foreign MNCs paid 87% of CT; top 10 paid 56% (2025); IDA employment 312,468

safeguards.residual_risk: The charter firms' lobby stays inside the republic. They can still leave, and booked profits can move instantly.

strongest_critique.liberal: Any charter regime raises political risk and will deter investment regardless of its terms.
strongest_critique.left: Charters legitimise the continued exploitation of Irish workers by US capital.

nodes.name_ga: An Banc Poiblí agus Comhar Creidmheasa
nodes.summary: A public bank in every county plus credit unions and co-operative banks. The main source of credit for co-ops, social enterprises, housing and the transition.
powers: Lend
Hold deposits

safeguards.mechanism: Lending by published criteria. Hard budgets apply to the bank too.
safeguards.residual_risk: Political lending, the classic failure of state banks.

strongest_critique.liberal: State banks lend by connection, not merit.

nodes.summary: Socially useful work at a living wage, in care, repair, retrofit, restoration, culture and public works, for anyone who wants it, near home.
powers: Offer work to all who seek it
Retrain workers from closed enterprises

safeguards.mechanism: Society, not the firm, holds the job guarantee, so enterprises can face hard budgets without workers facing destitution. It also absorbs those shut out by insider co-ops.
safeguards.residual_risk: Make-work with low morale and low productivity.

strongest_critique.liberal: A guaranteed job at a living wage sets a floor that undermines labour discipline.
strongest_critique.market: Fiscal cost scales with every closure.

nodes.summary: Universal childcare, home care and residential care; an income for home carers; and a national time-use survey every five years so care is counted and planned.
powers: Provide childcare, home care and residential care
Pay carers' income
Commission time-use surveys

safeguards.mechanism: Care is counted (time-use survey), planned, and well paid. Choice between public and family care, with support either way. Non-transferable parental leave for each parent.
safeguards.residual_risk: Underfunding relative to 'productive' investment, exactly as in the Eastern Bloc.

strongest_critique.liberal: Universal state childcare crowds out family choice and community provision.
strongest_critique.market: Very expensive.
strongest_critique.left: Paying for care turns family relationships into wage relationships (Federici's dilemma).

nodes.name_ga: Comhairle na nEalaíon agus an Dearaidh
nodes.summary: Funds the arts, crafts, design and public amenity at arm's length, with a budget floor. One per cent of public capital budgets goes to design and amenity.
powers: Fund the arts and design at arm's length

safeguards.mechanism: Morris's 'ornamental part of life' with a protected budget: beauty is not the first thing cut.
safeguards.residual_risk: Arm's-length bodies develop house styles and clienteles.

strongest_critique.liberal: Publicly funded art serves the funders' taste.
strongest_critique.left: Socialist-realist commissions began with good intentions too.

nodes.summary: Counter-espionage and protection of infrastructure only. No power to arrest, detain or prosecute; warrants from a judge; a published budget; citizens can see their files.
powers: Gather intelligence under judicial warrant

safeguards.mechanism: No powers of punishment, judicial warrants, full-access oversight by lot, a published budget, and a right to see one's own file.

precedent.text: Cheka from investigation to punishment within months
Stasi files opened after 1990 (Act to be sourced)

safeguards.residual_risk: A real hostile intelligence threat (Chile) may expose the limits of a weak service, and pressure to strengthen it will come in a crisis.

strongest_critique.left: Any secret service will eventually serve those in power.

nodes.summary: Independent. Advises on and enforces the physical budgets set by the Assembly, with a veto over any plan item or charter that would breach them, reviewable only by the Constitutional Court.
powers: Advise on physical budgets
Monitor compliance
Veto plan items or charters that breach budgets
nodes.composition: 9 members appointed by 3 judges + 6 members of the Citizens' Chamber; scientists, farmers, sector workers, public

safeguards.mechanism: The independent institution Soviet planning lacked. Democracy sets the limits; the Authority enforces them.

precedent.text: Aral Sea; Feshbach & Friendly, Ecocide in the USSR

safeguards.residual_risk: Budgets can be set loosely by the Assembly. An unelected veto will be resented, especially by farmers.

strongest_critique.liberal: Technocrats with a veto over economic plans is a recipe for unaccountable rule.
strongest_critique.market: Quantity caps ignore costs and substitution; prices would do the job better.
strongest_critique.left: Ecological technocracy depoliticises a class question: who pays for the transition.

nodes.summary: Independent. It licenses broadcasting, enforces ownership limits and accuracy in news, and appoints a third of the Public Media Trust board. It may not regulate opinion.
powers: License broadcasting
Enforce ownership limits
Administer media vouchers

safeguards.mechanism: Pluralism by ownership limits and citizen-directed media vouchers. The State never chooses which voices are heard.

precedent.text: Kern & Hainmueller: openness stabilised the GDR

safeguards.residual_risk: An 'accuracy' remit can creep into regulating opinion.

strongest_critique.liberal: Any regulator of news is a censor in waiting.

nodes.summary: Holds windfall revenues, including corporation tax above trend, to finance the transition, the Co-operative Development Fund and long-term investment. It cannot fund current spending.
powers: Invest for the long term
Finance the transition and co-op development

safeguards.mechanism: Windfall corporation tax, dependent on a few US firms, is ring-fenced *before* any change, so that its loss is survivable.
safeguards.residual_risk: Raids on the fund in hard times.

strongest_critique.liberal: Sovereign funds become political slush funds.

nodes.summary: Protects language rights, including the material rights in the Gaeltacht (housing, jobs, services), and can take enforcement proceedings.
powers: Enforce language rights in court

safeguards.mechanism: Material rather than symbolic support for Irish: daily speakers outside education numbered about 72,000 in 2022.
safeguards.residual_risk: Enforcement cannot create speakers.

strongest_critique.liberal: Compulsion breeds resentment of the language.

nodes.summary: Public broadcasting and digital media, funded as a fixed share of national income for ten years at a time. The board is a third staff, a third chosen by lot and a third appointed by the regulator.
powers: Editorial independence

safeguards.mechanism: No state monopoly on truth: funding cannot be cut as pressure, and no party executive member may sit on the board.
safeguards.residual_risk: A cosy staff consensus. Plural media funding is the counterweight.

strongest_critique.liberal: Public media crowd out private journalism.

nodes.summary: Neutral territorial, sea, air and undersea defence, and UN peacekeeping under the triple lock. No role in any political or industrial dispute.
powers: Defend territory, airspace, seas and undersea infrastructure
Peacekeeping under UN mandate with Executive and Assembly approval

safeguards.mechanism: Civilian control requiring 2/3 consent to senior appointments; a constitutional ban on any domestic political role; a duty to refuse unlawful orders.
safeguards.residual_risk: Officers' loyalty cannot be legislated. Chile's commander had sworn loyalty too.

strongest_critique.left: A professional army separate from the armed people is the Commune's first lesson ignored.
